g-pos-06.reason: The gap modifies the comparative adjective 'easier' inside 'made it ___ easier for staff to ...', so only an adverb fits: 'dramatically easier'. 'dramatic' (adjective) cannot pre-modify a comparative; 'drama' (noun) and 'dramatize' (verb) are impossible in this slot.
g-pos-06.why: Classic ETS part-of-speech item: anticipatory 'it' + adverb + comparative. The sentence is business-neutral, the tail clause adds realistic context without affecting the answer, and the four options are a clean word family.
g-pos-06.editorNote: Note that g-pos-07 in the same set is also an adverb-of-manner item; if these appear in one test form, consider making one of them a noun or adjective target to vary the family coverage.

g-pos-07.reason: The gap modifies the verb phrase 'can find the Pembry Conference Center', so the adverb 'easily' is required. 'find X easy' is possible only in the sense 'consider X to be easy', which makes no sense with a building as the object; 'ease' and 'easiness' are nouns and have no slot here.
g-pos-07.why: Standard adverb-after-object pattern seen often in Part 5. Adversarial reading of 'find ... easy' fails on meaning, so no careful editor would accept it. Lexical context (signs, directions, conference center) is typical TOEIC.

g-tense-06.reason: 'when she retires at the end of next month' sets a future reference point, and 'for thirty-two years' measures duration up to that point, so the future perfect 'will have been' is required. 'has been' would need a present reference point (and clashes with 'when she retires'); 'had been' needs a past reference point; 'was' is incompatible with a future 'when' clause.
g-tense-06.why: Future perfect with a present-tense 'when' clause is a genuine ETS tense target and the distractors are the usual set. The non-restrictive relative clause lengthens the stem but mirrors real TOEIC sentence shapes. No second option survives careful reading.

g-connect-06.reason: The main clause states a positive allowance ('will accept deliveries after that time') that depends on a condition ('the driver has arranged access ... in advance'), so 'provided that' is the only logical connector. 'unless' reverses the logic (accepting deliveries unless access was arranged is absurd); 'even if' makes the arrangement irrelevant, contradicting the 'staffed only until 5 p.m.' rationale; 'so that' would make the arrangement a purpose of accepting deliveries, which is backwards.
g-connect-06.why: Good conjunction item with a conditional-vs-concessive contrast that ETS uses. One small stylistic wobble: the opening 'Because' clause explains a restriction, but the main clause is phrased as a permission, so the causal link reads slightly indirect. It does not open a second answer.
g-connect-06.fix: Optional: change 'Because' to 'Although' ('Although the loading dock is staffed only until 5 p.m., the warehouse will accept deliveries after that time provided that ...') for a tighter logical fit.
g-connect-06.editorNote: If 'Because' is kept, the item still works; the fix only improves naturalness.

g-prep-05.reason: 'labeled and stored ___ the guidelines set out in section 4' requires 'in accordance with' (following the guidelines). 'in response to the guidelines' is semantically odd for storage practice; 'in addition to the guidelines' would mean the chemicals are stored alongside the guidelines; 'in exchange for' is nonsensical.
g-prep-05.why: Multi-word preposition item exactly in the ETS mould; 'in accordance with' + guidelines/regulations is a high-frequency TOEIC collocation. The relative clause tail is a touch long but harmless.

g-mandative-03.reason: 'recommended ... that the accounts payable team ___ every invoice' takes the mandative subjunctive, so the base form 'check' is required. 'checked' is a past indicative; British English sometimes allows an indicative in a mandative clause, but the matrix verb is present perfect ('have recommended'), so the indicative would have to be 'checks', which is not offered, and 'checked' reads as a report of a past fact, which the context rejects. 'is checking' and 'checking' are not possible after 'recommend that'.
g-mandative-03.why: ETS tests the subjunctive after recommend/request/require regularly, usually with 'be'; using a lexical verb with a plural subject keeps the item fair while removing the giveaway of a visible -s. Distractors are well chosen.
g-mandative-03.editorNote: Adversarial British-English reading ('recommended that the team checked') was tested and rejected because of the present-perfect matrix verb; no change needed.

v-synonym-02.reason: The second clause ('borrowers must return the equipment within two weeks') shows the department is the lender, so 'lends laptops and projectors to staff' is correct. 'borrows ... to staff' is ungrammatical and semantically reversed; 'returns ... to staff' conflicts with staff being the ones who return equipment; 'donates' is incompatible with a return requirement.
v-synonym-02.why: Clear lend/borrow contrast with a decisive second clause; this is a plausible lower-band vocabulary item. The word 'borrowers' in the stem slightly telegraphs the answer, which keeps the item easy.
v-synonym-02.editorNote: If a harder version is wanted, replace 'borrowers' with 'staff' so the clue comes only from 'return'.

v-family-07.reason: 'praise the staff for being ___ to guests' needs' requires the adjective 'attentive', which collocates with 'to ... needs'. 'attendant' as an adjective means 'accompanying' (attendant risks) and does not take 'to needs'; 'attended' would make the staff the recipients of attention; 'attending' means present at an event or (medically) treating, neither of which fits.
v-family-07.why: Word-family item with an adjective target and a strong collocation ('attentive to needs'); 'attendant' is a well-chosen trap for test-takers who recognise the stem only. Hospitality context is standard TOEIC.

overall: All eight items resolve to a single unambiguous answer; adversarial readings (flat-adverb 'easy', British indicative 'checked', 'attendant to') fail on grammar or meaning, so no item is ambiguous. The set sits at easy-to-medium difficulty with authentic TOEIC phrasing; the only suggestions are optional polish (Because/Although in g-connect-06, the 'borrowers' clue in v-synonym-02) and variety, since two of the three grammar-pos items both target adverbs.
